security_audit.summary: All 290 static detections are false positives from documentation, ordinary JavaScript examples, and reference links. No evidence found of malicious execution, credential exfiltration, or prompt injection. One medium-severity guidance issue recommends passing a raw session cookie to a logging function, which could expose credentials when adopted.

remediation.issue: The recommended non-blocking logging example passes the raw session-id cookie to logUserAction.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the session cookie with an approved non-secret correlation identifier. Update the compiled guide and corresponding rule example, and explicitly prohibit logging authentication cookies.

- `async-cheap-condition-before-await` - Check cheap sync conditions before awaiting flags or remote
- `async-defer-await` - Move await into branches where actually used
- `async-api-routes` - Start promises early, await late in API routes
- `bundle-analyzable-paths` - Prefer statically analyzable import and file-system paths to avoid bro
- `bundle-conditional` - Load modules only when feature is activated
- `bundle-preload` - Preload on hover/focus for perceived speed
- `server-auth-actions` - Authenticate server actions like API routes
- `server-cache-lru` - Use LRU cache for cross-request caching
- `server-dedup-props` - Avoid duplicate serialization in RSC props
- `server-hoist-static-io` - Hoist static I/O (fonts, logos) to module level
- `server-no-shared-module-state` - Avoid module-level mutable request state in RSC/SSR
- `server-serialization` - Minimize data passed to client components
- `server-parallel-nested-fetching` - Chain nested fetches per item in Promise.all
- `client-swr-dedup` - Use SWR for automatic request deduplication
- `rerender-defer-reads` - Don't subscribe to state only used in callbacks
- `rerender-memo` - Extract expensive work into memoized components
- `rerender-derived-state` - Subscribe to derived booleans, not raw values
- `rerender-derived-state-no-effect` - Derive state during render, not effects
- `rerender-functional-setstate` - Use functional setState for stable callbacks
- `rerender-lazy-state-init` - Pass function to useState for expensive values
- `rerender-move-effect-to-event` - Put interaction logic in event handlers
- `rerender-use-deferred-value` - Defer expensive renders to keep input responsive
- `rerender-use-ref-transient-values` - Use refs for transient frequent values
- `rendering-animate-svg-wrapper` - Animate div wrapper, not SVG element
- `rendering-hydration-no-flicker` - Use inline script for client-only data
- `rendering-resource-hints` - Use React DOM resource hints for preloading
- `rendering-script-defer-async` - Use defer or async on script tags
- `js-batch-dom-css` - Group CSS changes via classes or cssText
- `js-cache-function-results` - Cache function results in module-level Map
- `js-combine-iterations` - Combine multiple filter/map into one loop
- `js-length-check-first` - Check array length before expensive comparison
- `js-min-max-loop` - Use loop for min/max instead of sort
- `js-flatmap-filter` - Use flatMap to map and filter in one pass
- `js-request-idle-callback` - Defer non-critical work to browser idle time
- `advanced-effect-event-deps` - Don't put `useEffectEvent` results in effect deps
- `advanced-init-once` - Initialize app once per app load
- `bundle-analyzable-paths` - Prefer statically analyzable import and file-system paths to avoid bro
- `server-dedup-props` - Avoid duplicate serialization in RSC props
- `server-no-shared-module-state` - Avoid module-level mutable request state in RSC/SSR
- `js-flatmap-filter` - Use flatMap to map and filter in one pass

content.value_statement: Sequential requests, large bundles, and unnecessary renders can slow React applications. This skill guides AI assistants through prioritized React and Next.js improvements with practical examples.
actual_capabilities: Identify sequential asynchronous work and recommend concurrency patterns that preserve data dependencies.
Suggest dynamic imports, conditional loading, and import-path changes to reduce initial bundle work.
Guide server-side caching, request deduplication, and smaller Server Component payloads.
Review component identity, effect dependencies, derived state, and functional updates to reduce unnecessary renders.
Recommend Suspense boundaries, resource hints, deferred rendering, and browser layout optimizations.
Explain authentication checks for Server Actions and request-data isolation during server rendering.
limitations: Provides written guidelines, not an executable profiler, benchmark runner, or automatic enforcement engine.
Some recommendations depend on React, Next.js, browser, and compiler versions.
Performance gains require application-specific measurement and are not guaranteed.
Examples need security review before adoption, including replacing raw session-cookie logging with a non-secret identifier.

use_cases.title: Review Component Performance
use_cases.description: Check a component change for redundant effects, unstable props, repeated computation, and accidental remounts.

use_cases.title: Improve Server Data Loading
use_cases.description: Review Next.js routes for asynchronous waterfalls, oversized client props, and incorrectly scoped request data.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Optimization Work
use_cases.description: Organize review findings by impact and select changes for measurement before broader team adoption.

prompt_templates.title: Explain One Performance Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React component using the skill guidelines. Explain the highest-impact issue and one focused improvement. Preserve behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Remove Independent Request Delays
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Next.js route for sequential requests. Identify dependencies and parallelize only independent operations. Preserve authentication, authorization, and error behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Review Bundle Loading
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect these imports and component boundaries. Recommend selective loading and preloading that fit our framework version. Explain tradeoffs and propose bundle measurements.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Measured Application Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the supplied React and Next.js files across the eight rule categories. Rank evidence-backed findings by impact. Preserve security boundaries and propose regression tests.

output_examples.input: Review a route that loads account details, preferences, and notifications sequentially.
output: Finding: Preferences and notifications wait unnecessarily if they do not depend on account details.
Recommendation: Start independent requests together after any required authorization checks.
Verification: Compare request timing and confirm unchanged error handling.

output_examples.input: Review a search component that filters a large list whenever the input changes.
output: Finding: Filtering and rendering the results may delay input updates.
Recommendation: Consider deferred input for the expensive results and memoize work using that deferred value.
Verification: Measure input responsiveness and confirm results update correctly.

output_examples.input: Review a page that imports a large editor before users open its editing panel.
output: Finding: The editor contributes work before the editing panel is needed.
Recommendation: Load the editor on demand and consider preloading when the opening control receives focus.
Verification: Compare initial bundle size and panel opening latency.

best_practices: Prioritize request waterfalls and bundle loading before smaller JavaScript optimizations.
Check framework versions, rendering boundaries, and security requirements before applying any example.
Measure changes with representative workloads and run regression tests.
anti_patterns: Parallelizing dependent operations or moving protected data access before authorization.
Adding memoization and caches everywhere without measuring costs or planning invalidation.
Copying examples without reviewing credential handling, tenant isolation, and runtime compatibility.

faq.question: What does this skill provide?
faq.answer: It provides prioritized React and Next.js guidelines, incorrect and corrected examples, and references for AI-assisted development and review.

faq.question: Which assistants can use it?
faq.answer: The marketplace listing supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. The skill itself consists of written instructions and reference files.

faq.question: Does it run performance tests automatically?
faq.answer: No. It guides analysis and suggested changes. Profiling, benchmarks, and regression testing require your project tools.

faq.question: Do the rules apply to every React project?
faq.answer: No. Some rules depend on Next.js server features, newer React APIs, or browser support. Check your runtime and compiler configuration.

faq.question: Which improvements should I address first?
faq.answer: Start with request waterfalls and bundle size. Use measurements to decide whether rendering and JavaScript optimizations matter for your application.

faq.question: Can I copy the examples directly into production?
faq.answer: Review and adapt them first. Preserve authorization and data isolation, avoid logging session credentials, and test behavior in your environment.
